sentence: This project studies a mouse that shows a rare neurological disease seen in patients and tests a gene therapy in it.
This project studies ways to make certain immune cells less suppressive so that cancer immunotherapy works better in solid cancer models.
This project brings together physics, biology, mathematics and chemistry to look for earlier diagnosis and more specific treatments of disease.
This project studies how high-risk human papillomaviruses enter cells.
This project studies how interferon-induced transmembrane proteins block viruses from entering cells, using imaging and biophysical methods.
This project builds a synthetic polymer like collagen that could replace collagen from animals in tissue engineering, drug delivery and wound healing.
This project studies how weak inhibitory control and its neural basis affect people with traumatic stress in everyday life.
This project studies how tumors and the immune system change together as cancer spreads, and how tumors escape immune responses.
This project studies how nerves pass their mitochondria to breast cancer cells and what happens to the cancer cells as a result.
This project studies how double-negative T cells fight breast cancer growth.
This project studies two types of glioblastoma tumor and builds mouse models of them to test possible therapeutic targets.
This project tries to find out whether losing a gene for an actin-binding protein helps the immune system fight breast cancer.
This project studies how heme, an iron-containing nutrient, acts as a signal between parts of cells and organs to control lifespan.
This project supplies clinically annotated samples such as tumor, plasma and serum to researchers.
This project tests a team approach to testing tumors so more rural patients with cancer receive targeted therapies.
This project builds software tools that use genome sequence data to predict the metabolic pathways of disease-causing bacteria.
This project builds a community that shares big data methods to help understand, diagnose and treat cancer.
This project builds a single gene editing method that corrects the genetic errors behind a heart condition called familial dilated cardiomyopathy.
This project studies the structure of a glycine receptor and its lipidic profile to understand its role in neurogenesis and neurodevelopmental disorders.
